summary: Client SDK connection priority inversion + retry sequencing causing apparent request stalls/long-tail latency
description: Issue summary: Since 2026-03-09 ~09:00 UTC, multiple ShoplineAI endpoints are reporting long-tail inference latency (95th/99th spikes to 5-30s) and intermittent client-side timeouts. Impact: Customer storefront personalization flows experience timeouts leading to lost recommendations during peak traffic windows. Environment: Redwood hosted API, ShoplineAI on Dedicated pool in us-east-1, using Redwood JS SDK v1.11.0 with default pool settings. Observed behavior: SDK logs show serialized retries holding a connection slot while backoff timers run, then attempting to send which causes head-of-line blocking. Expected behavior: SDK should retry without blocking healthy sockets or should use new connections when backoffs are active so other requests are not queued behind retried requests.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Install Redwood JS SDK v1.11.0 and configure with connectionPool.max=8 and keepAlive=true.
2) Reproduce with a high-rate workload: concurrent 50 requests to /v1/generate pinned to redwood/gpt-7b-v1-quant in us-east-1.
3) Intentionally inject transient 503 responses from a backend serving instance (we provided a test harness).
4) Observe client-side request queueing and long-tail latency spikes; SDK logs show retries occupying pool slots during backoff intervals.

comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel (Support): Initial report received from ShoplineAI CS. Included SDK logs and sample reproduction harness. Customer reports regression after upgrading from v1.10.4 to v1.11.0.

2026-03-10 - Liam Gomez (SRE): Triaging. Reproduced locally with customer's harness; can see retries holding pool slots. Initial hypothesis: retry code path marks 'retainSocket=true' during backoff which prevents the socket from returning to pool.

2026-03-11 - Dev (Maya Chen): Reviewed SDK PR history; a change in PR#894 introduced keepSocketDuringBackoff flag to reduce TLS rehandshake costs. Suspect priority inversion: long-running retries keep sockets causing fresh requests to queue.

2026-03-11 - Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed spikes align with periods of transient 503 from a single serving node (noisy neighbor). They see immediate improvement when we asked them to downgrade to SDK v1.10.4 as a temporary measure.

2026-03-12 - Liam: Ran canary with SDK patch that sets retainSocket=false for retry backoff; 95th percentile latency returned to baseline under load. Need engineering sign-off to ship fix and backfill release notes.
2026-03-13 - Maya Chen (Engineer): Preparing PR to change default retry behavior to release socket on backoff and to add metrics for 'retry_holds_socket' and 'queue_wait_time_ms'.
investigation_notes: Timeline: 03-09 first customer alert; replicated 03-10. Root cause hypothesis: v1.11.0 change (PR#894) added optimization to keep sockets reserved across retries to avoid re-TLS/handshake cost. Under normal conditions this reduced tail latency. However, when the backend produced transient 5xxs at volume, SDK retry loops (with exponential backoff/jitter) held pool slots for the duration of backoff intervals. With a small connection pool (max=8) and bursty inbound load, healthy requests were queued behind sockets that were effectively sleeping, producing long tail latency and perceived timeouts. Evidence: SDK logs show queued_requests rising while backoff timers active; downgrading to v1.10.4 (no retain feature) eliminated the queueing. Simulated load with a patched SDK that returns sockets to pool during backoff showed baseline p95 performance.
resolution: Workaround provided: Customer rolled back to SDK v1.10.4 (recommended) and temporarily increased connectionPool.max to 20 to reduce contention. Long-term fix: Engineering to change default behavior in SDK to not retain socket while waiting for backoff; instead mark socket as reusable and attach retry metadata so the next retry can preferentially reuse a warm socket if available. Also ship observability changes: add 'retry_holds_socket' metric and an SDK health check to surface high queue_wait_time_ms. Patch PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/clients/pull/914. Planned release: v1.11.1 with fix and opt-in config for customers needing retainSocket semantics. Follow-up actions: update runbook 'connection-pool-troubleshooting', notify dedicated customers about the v1.11.1 rollout, and create an alert in Console when queue_wait_time_ms > 5000ms.
